questions.question: Explain how urbanisation increases flood risk. (4 marks)

points.text: Urbanisation increases flood risk because impermeable surfaces like tarmac and concrete prevent rainwater from infiltrating into the soil (1 mark), causing up to 95% of rainfall to become surface runoff compared to 10% in natural areas (1 mark). questions.question: Describe the features of a flashy storm hydrograph. (4 marks)

points.text: A flashy hydrograph has a steep rising limb showing that discharge increases rapidly after rainfall begins (1 mark). The peak discharge is high, meaning the river reaches a large volume of flow (1 mark). The lag time between peak rainfall and peak discharge is short, typically just a few hours (1 mark). questions.question: Compare hard and soft engineering strategies for managing flood risk. (6 marks)

points.text: Hard engineering uses artificial structures like dams and flood walls to control water and protect property (1 mark). Dams are very effective at regulating flow but are expensive (£20M+) and flood valleys upstream (1 mark). questions.question: Using a named example, assess the effectiveness of flood management strategies. (9 marks)

points.text: Cockermouth in Cumbria has experienced repeated flooding, most severely in 2009 and 2015.
